QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_8

question.text: Mr. Arjun Saxena is setting up a new pooled investment vehicle and seeks your view on AIF registration. Which of the following structures would be EXCLUDED from the SEBI AIF definition and therefore NOT require AIF registration?

answer.text: A close-ended pooled vehicle from 25 HNIs targeting unlisted mid-cap equity
An open-ended pooled vehicle from institutional investors investing in listed derivatives
A family trust set up for the Saxena family's own succession and wealth planning
A privately-pooled real estate debt fund with INR 200 crore corpus from 50 UHNIs

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, AIFs are defined as privately pooled investment vehicles that collect funds from select investors. The exclusions from the AIF definition expressly include private funds of a family and funds regulated under other regulators. A family trust set up for the family's own succession and wealth planning therefore falls outside the AIF definition and does not require AIF registration. The Trap: A close-ended pooled vehicle taking capital from 25 HNIs for unlisted equity is exactly the privately-pooled-from-select-investors profile the AIF definition captures. An open-ended pooled vehicle from institutional investors investing in listed derivatives is still externally pooled from select investors and not within the family-trust exclusion. A privately pooled real estate debt fund with INR 200 crore corpus from 50 UHNIs is similarly a textbook private AIF and not a family trust. Note: The exclusion turns on whether the pool is a family arrangement versus a private pool from external select investors — investor count alone does not decide AIF applicability.
